title: Drawing a graph in screen space
description: Optimising a graph's node positions directly in pixels, with a soft-argmax head borrowed from human pose estimation.
detail:
Third-year semester project, in a team of three, supervised by Romain Giot (LaBRI). We optimise the positions of a graph's nodes directly in pixels: the drawing is rendered differentiably through signed distance functions, the losses are computed on the image, and the gradient flows back to the weights of a recurrent GNN.

The idea I brought to it: a soft-argmax output head, borrowed from human pose estimation. A node's position becomes the weighted average of a probability map over pixels, differentiable, unlike an argmax, and always inside the frame by construction.

Work in progress.
